(p. 584) **Surah al-Mursalat**

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿By those sent forth in successive waves,﴾ ﴿by those that blow with violent blasts,﴾ ﴿by those that spread (clouds) far and wide,﴾ ﴿by those that separate decisively,﴾ ﴿by those that deliver a reminder,﴾ ﴿as an excuse or as a warning.﴾ Glorified and exalted is He, swears by groups of angels whom He sent with His commands. They blew violently in their passage. He also swears by groups of them who spread their wings in the air when descending with the revelation, or who spread the laws (sharai') on earth, or who revive dead souls (by sending them) disbelief and ignorance. With what they conveyed, they distinguish between truth and falsehood, and then they deliver a reminder to the prophets, peace be upon them, as an excuse for the righteous (muhiqqin) or as a warning for the falsifiers (mubtilin).

Or (the meaning is): He swears by winds of punishment, which He sent so that they blew violently, and by winds of mercy, which spread the clouds in the air and separated them, like His saying: ﴿and makes it into fragments﴾ [al-Rum: 48]. Then they deliver a reminder, either as an excuse for those who turn to Allah in repentance and seek His forgiveness when they see the blessing of Allah in the rain and thank Him for it, or as a warning for those who do not give thanks and attribute that to the stars (anwa'). They are described as "those that deliver a reminder" on account of their being the cause (of it).

"ʿurfan" (ﻋُﺮْﻓًﺎ) is a circumstantial accusative (ḥāl), meaning "in succession," like the mane of a horse (ʿurf al-faras), one following another. Or it is an accusative of purpose (mafʿūl lahu), meaning they were sent for benevolence and goodness (al-maʿrūf). "ʿaṣfan" (ﻋَﺼْﻔًﺎ) and "nashran" (ﻧَﺸْﺮًا) are verbal nouns (maṣdar). 

"Aw nudhran" (ﺃَﻭْ ﻧُﺬْﺭًا) is read with sukun by Abu ʿAmr and the Kufan readers other than Abu Bakr and Hammad. "Al-ʿudhr" (ﺍﻟْﻌُﺬْﺭُ) and "al-nudhr" (ﺍﻟﻨُّﺬْﺭُ) are both verbal nouns: from ʿadhara (ﻋَﺬَﺭَ), when one erases an offence, and from andhara (ﺃَﻧْﺬَﺭَ), when one warns of an act. They are like "al-kufr" (ﺍﻟْﻛُﻔْﺮُ) and "al-shukr" (ﺍﻟﺸُّﻛْﺮُ). (p. 585) Their being in the accusative is either as a substitute (badal) for "dhikran" or as an accusative of purpose (mafʿūl lahu).

Verse 7: ﴿Indeed, what you are promised﴾ — that which you are promised of the coming of the Day of Resurrection,

﴿is surely going to occur﴾ — it will certainly happen, will descend, there is no doubt about it. It is the answer to the oath (jawab al-qasam), and there is no pause here, so that the answer is joined to the oath.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 77, verse 8:

﴿Then when the stars are obliterated﴾, i.e., effaced, or their light is taken away. The answer (jawab) of "fa-idha" (then when) is omitted, and the element governing it (al-'amil fihā) is its answer, which is the occurrence of the Decisive Separation (al-fasl) or the like. And "al-nujum" (the stars) is the subject (fa'il) of a verb that is explained by "tumisat" (obliterated), which is the verb governing it.
﴿And when the sky is opened﴾, it is split open, and becomes gateways.
﴿And when the mountains are blown away﴾: they are uprooted from their places.

﴿And when the Messengers are brought to their appointed time﴾. That is: وُقِّتَتْ (wuqqitat), as in the recitation (qira'ah) of Abu 'Amr, and the hamza was substituted for the waw. The meaning of the appointing of the Messengers is clarifying the time at which they attend to bear witness against their nations.

﴿For what Day were they postponed?﴾ They were delayed and given respite. The phrasing magnifies the Day and expresses wonder at its terror. Al-ta'jil (postponement) derives from al-ajal (term, appointed time), just as al-tawqit (fixing a time) derives from al-waqt (time).

Tafsir of Surah 77 (al-Mursalat), verse 13:

﴿For the Day of Decision﴾. It is an explanation of "the Day of Postponement," and it is the day on which the creatures are separated (judged) among one another.
"And what will make you know what the Day of Decision is?" This is another expression of wonder and of the magnitude of its matter.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 77, verse 15:

﴿Woe﴾ [al-Mursalat: 19], is the subject (mubtada'), and although it is indefinite (nakira), it is permissible because, in its origin, it is a verbal noun in the accusative (masdar mansub) that stands in place of its verb (sadd masadda fi'lih). However, it has been shifted to the nominative (raf') to indicate the meaning of the constancy of destruction and its perpetuity for the one against whom it is invoked. A similar example is: ﴿Peace be upon you﴾ [al-Ra'd: 24].

﴿On that day﴾ is its adverbial complement (zarf).

﴿for the deniers﴾ is its predicate (khabar), referring to that day.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 77, verse 16:

﴿Did We not destroy the former peoples?﴾ — the earlier nations who had passed away and who denied (their messengers).

{Then We shall follow them up with the later ones.} This is a fresh sentence after a pause, and it is a threat to the people of Makkah, meaning: Then We shall deal with their like among the later ones in the same way as We dealt with the earlier ones, because they denied in the same manner as those denied.

Thus (is it): like that heinous deed,

﴿We do to the criminals﴾, to everyone who committed crime.
﴿Woe on that day to the deniers﴾, [referring to] what We have threatened.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 77, verse 20:

﴿Did We not create you from a despised fluid?﴾ Lowly, insignificant; it is the nutfah (a small drop of seminal fluid).

﴿So We placed it﴾ — i.e., the water —

﴿in a firm abode﴾, a resting place in which it is secured, namely the womb, and a place of settling.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 77, verse 22:

﴿Until a known term﴾. Al-ḥāl (the state/condition), i.e., deferred until a known measure of time, which Allah has known and decreed, and it is nine months, or more than that, or less than that.

﴿So We determined﴾, meaning We determined it as a determining.

﴿and how excellent are the determiners﴾, meaning how excellent are We as the ones who determine it! Or, "So We determined over that", and then ﴿how excellent are the capable ones﴾, meaning how excellent are We as the ones capable over it! The first interpretation is more worthy, because of the qira'a (canonical mode of recitation) of Nafi' and Ali with tashdid (doubling of the letter), reading "fa-qaddarna" (فقدّرنا), and because of His saying: ﴿from a drop of sperm He created him and ordained him﴾ [Abasa: 19].

Woe on that day to those who deny. (Surah al-Mursalat 77:24)

Woe to them for denying the blessing of the innate nature (al-fitrah).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 77, verse 25:

﴿Have We not made the earth a receptacle,﴾ It derives from "kafata al-shay'" (he gathered and drew the thing together), meaning when he gathered it and brought it together. It is the name of that which gathers (kafit), like their saying "al-dimam" (that which gathers together), for what gathers together. And it is in the accusative (intasaba) by it.

﴿Alive and dead﴾. It is as if it were said: "gathering [them] alive and dead," or [it is governed] by a verb implied by "kifatan" (gathering), which is "takfit" (it gathers): it gathers the living upon its back and the dead in its belly. The indefiniteness in both words is for magnification, meaning: "it gathers living [creatures] that cannot be counted, and dead [ones] that cannot be enumerated."

﴿And We placed therein firmly fixed mountains﴾, meaning mountains that are fixed and steady,

﴿towering high﴾, meaning lofty,

﴿and We gave you to drink sweet water﴾, meaning fresh and sweet.
﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers,﴾ of this blessing.

Qur'an 77:29: "Proceed to that which you used to deny."

That is, it will be said to the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection: "Proceed to the Fire which you used to deny."

(p-587) ﴿Proceed﴾: a repetition for emphasis.

﴿to a shadow﴾: the smoke of Hell.

﴿with three branches﴾: because of its immensity, it branches into three branches; likewise, the great smoke divides into three groups.

﴿Lā ẓalīl﴾ (no shade): an adjective (naʿt) qualifying "ẓill" (shade), meaning: not providing shade from the heat of that Day and the heat of the Fire.

﴿Wa lā yughnī﴾ (nor does it avail): in the place of a genitive (maḥall al-jarr), meaning: and not availing them anything, ﴿min al-lahab﴾ (against the flame), i.e., against the heat of the flame.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 77, verse 32:

﴿Indeed, it﴾, i.e., the Fire,

﴿throws up sparks﴾, which is what flies off from the fire,

﴿like a palace﴾, in its size. It was said: it is the thick part of trees, whose singular is "qasrah".

﴿As if it were camels﴾. "The Kufan [reciters] except Abu Bakr [read it as] *jimalat*," the plural of *jamal* (camel), "*jimalat*." "Others [read it as] *jimalat*," which is the plural of the plural (*jam' al-jam'*). "*Ṣufr*" is the plural of *aṣfar*, meaning black tending toward yellow. He likened the sparks to *qusur* (palaces) because of their great size and height, and to *jimal* (camels) because of their size, length, and color.

Woe on that Day to the deniers. (Qur'an 77:34)

This is the description of it.

This is the day when they will not speak. It is also read with the word "day" in the accusative (naṣb), meaning: what has been related to you is occurring on that day. Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, was asked about this verse and about His words: ﴿Then, indeed, on the Day of Resurrection you will dispute before your Lord﴾ [al-Zumar: 31]. He said: "On that day there are standing-places; in some of them they dispute, and in some of them they do not speak," or (it means) they do not speak in a way that benefits them, so their speaking is treated as if it were "no speech."

"And it will not be permitted for them" to make excuses,

"so they will not offer excuse." It is coordinated (ʿaṭf) upon "is permitted" (yuʾdhanu), enrolled within the string of negation (silk al-nafy); meaning: there will be for them neither permission nor excuse.
﴿Woe on that Day to those who deny﴾, [who deny] this Day.

﴿This is the Day of Decision﴾, between the one in the right and the one in the wrong, the doer of good and the doer of evil, through recompense. (p-588) ﴿We have gathered you﴾, O deniers of Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿and the former peoples﴾, and the deniers before you.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 77, verse 39:

﴿If you have any scheme﴾, a stratagem for averting the punishment,

﴿then scheme against Me﴾, that is, devise plans against Me for saving yourselves from the punishment. The word "الْكَيْدُ" (al-kayd, scheming) is transitive. You say "كِدْتُ فُلانًا" (kidtu fulanan, "I schemed against so-and-so"), meaning that you plotted against him.
﴿Woe on that Day to those who deny,﴾ [i.e., those who deny] the Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 77, verse 41:

﴿Indeed, the God-fearing﴾, from the punishment of Allah,

﴿in shades﴾, the plural of "ẓill" (shade),

﴿and springs﴾, flowing in Paradise.
{And fruits of what they desire} — i.e., delicious fruits that are desired.

"Eat and drink" (﴿كُلُوا واشْرَبُوا﴾) is in the position of a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring back to the pronoun in "the God-conscious" (al-muttaqīn), within the adverbial phrase "in shades" (fī ẓilāl): that is, they are settled in shades, and it is said to them that.

"Wholesome and pleasant it is for you, for what you used to do" (﴿هَنِيئًا بِما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾): [this refers to what you did] in the world (al-dunyā).

Verse-level translation with the surrounding commentary text:

﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good.﴾ So do good, and you will be rewarded with this.
﴿Woe on that Day to those who deny,﴾ that is, deny Paradise.

Eat and enjoy yourselves, [for a] little while; indeed you are criminals.

This is a resumed statement (kalam mustanaf), addressed to the deniers in the world, in the manner of a threat, like His saying: ﴿Do whatever you will﴾ [Fussilat: 40]. ﴿A little while﴾, because the enjoyment of the world is little.

﴿Indeed you are criminals﴾, i.e., disbelievers. That is: every criminal eats and enjoys himself for a few days, then remains in everlasting destruction.
"Woe on that day to the deniers"—(of the blessings).

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 77, verse 48:**

﴿And when it is said to them, "Bow down,"⁠﴾ — humble yourselves before God, and submit yourselves to Him by accepting His revelation and following His religion, and abandon this arrogance.

﴿They do not bow down.⁠﴾ — They do not humble themselves, they do not accept that, and they persist in their arrogance. And when it is said to them, "Pray," they do not pray.
﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers!﴾, [the deniers] of the command and the prohibition.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 77, verse 50:

﴿So in what discourse after it will they believe?﴾, after the Qur'an,

﴿will they believe﴾: that is, if they do not believe in the Qur'an, despite its being a clear sign (āyah mubṣirah), and a dazzling miracle (muʿjizah bāhirah), among the heavenly Books, so in what Book after it will they believe?!
